article_title: Online-to-offline combined with problem-based learning is an effective teaching modality in the standardized residency training of nephrology.
citation: Wu Junxia, Ke You, Chen Zhida, Alhendi Mhd Alaa, Zhu Lina, Ma Kunling. (2024). Online-to-offline combined with problem-based learning is an effective teaching modality in the standardized residency training of nephrology. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05675-w
title: O2O/PBL teaching process for nephrology residency training (Ding Talk platform with pre-class materials, in-class problem-based study groups, and post-class live playback)
description: The article describes a blended teaching process combining online and offline components: instructors upload "online teaching materials such as operation and theoretical courses" and "specific clinical problems" for roughly 30 minutes of pre-class self-study; during class, trainees in study groups of 2 to 3 discuss the pre-class problems while Ding Talk live broadcast runs alongside face-to-face teaching on smart electronic screens; after class, live playback is available for repeated viewing. The LBT comparison group received traditional classroom teaching with no pre-class materials, no problem-based discussion, and no live broadcast.
requirements: Attending nephrologist instructors with at least 3 years of department experience, regularly trained in the teaching methods
Smart electronic screens in the classroom and the Ding Talk network platform for material distribution and live broadcasting
Teaching content formulated according to the residency training teaching syllabus in China
constraints: The article states the online workload was calibrated so the amount of online work was comparable to the time needed to review course material with the LBT group
target_learners: Internal medicine residency trainees rotating through nephrology
target_learning_goals: Practical skills such as urinary catheterization
Clinical thinking including diagnosis and treatment planning
examples: Trainees were divided into study groups of 2 to 3, discussed problems raised before class, and the teacher gave feedback and summarized the questions
